extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners handling petitions to revive abandoned applications (37 CFR 1.137)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing, and evaluating petitions to revive abandoned (including provisional) patent applications under 37 CFR 1.137, and related procedural requirements (e.g., terminal disclaimers, reconsideration, public access).

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing of unavoidable delay (37 CFR 1.137(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) must show to the satisfaction of the Director that the entire delay in filing the required reply from the due date for the reply until the filing of a grantable petition was unavoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.137(a)(3) requires the applicant to carry the burden of proof in every petition under 1.137(a) to establish that the delay from the due date until filing a grantable petition was unavoidable. Applicant must show how the delay occurred despite exercise of due care/diligence; failure to establish that the entire delay was unavoidable may lead to denial regardless of original circumstances of abandonment (see Application of Haines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing of unintentional delay (37 CFR 1.137(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.137(b) must be accompanied by a statement that the entire delay in providing the required reply from the due date until the filing of a grantable petition was unintentional, and the Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While generally only the statement that the entire delay was unintentional is required, the Office may require the applicant to carry the burden of proof to establish that the delay was unintentional (within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7) and 37 CFR 1.137(b)) when there is doubt as to whether the entire delay was unintentional (see Application of G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Party whose delay is relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: The relevant delay under 37 CFR 1.137 is that of the party who had the right or authority to reply to avoid abandonment; the applicant's delay is irrelevant if the applicant assigned the entire right, title, and interest or ceded control of prosecution to a third party (unless reassigned prior to the due date or the third party acts only in a fiduciary capacity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the inventor/applicant assigned the application to a third party (e.g., employer) and the third party decides not to file, the applicant’s actions/intentions are irrelevant (see Kim v. Quigg). Similarly, where a third party controls prosecution, its decisions bind the applicant (see Winkler). An agreement that gives a third party unbridled discretion to prosecute will bind the applicant unless the contract expressly limits prosecution to a fiduciary role (see Futures Technology Ltd. v. Quigg).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirement (37 CFR 1.137(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.137(a) or (b) must be accompanied by a terminal disclaimer (and fee) in specified categories of applications and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimers are required for: (A) design applications; (B) nonprovisional utility applications (other than reissue) filed before June 8, 1995; (C) nonprovisional plant applications (other than reissue) filed before June 8, 1995. Additionally, utility or plant applications filed on or after June 8, 1995 but before May 29, 2000 require a terminal disclaimer if abandoned during appeal, during interference, or while under a secrecy order (because of URAA patent term extension eligibility). The disclaimer must dedicate to the public a terminal part of patent term equivalent to the period of abandonment (subject to special rules for utility/plant applications filed before June 8, 1995). The requirement does not apply to: revivals sought solely for purposes of copendency with an application filed on/after June 8, 1995; lapsed patents; reissue applications; or reexamination proceedings. The Office will not state the period disclaimed in its decision granting revival because that period cannot be determined at the time of grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer is distinct from delay showing; not a substitute
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing a terminal disclaimer is not a substitute for establishing that the delay was unavoidable (1.137(a)) or unintentional (1.137(b)), nor does an unavoidable/unintentional delay waive the terminal disclaimer requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement that the entire delay be unavoidable or at least unintentional is distinct from the terminal disclaimer requirement; the filing of a terminal disclaimer cannot excuse an intentional delay in filing a petition, nor will an unavoidable/unintentional delay permit waiver of the terminal disclaimer requirement (see Application of Takao).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for waiver of terminal disclaimer (37 CFR 1.183)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant considers the terminal disclaimer requirement inappropriate, applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 (with fee) requesting waiver of the 1.137(d) requirement, in toto or to the extent it exceeds the applicant's considered appropriate period of disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants of such 1.183 petitions are strictly limited to situations showing an 'extraordinary situation' in which 'justice requires' the requested relief (e.g., abandonment caused no actual delay in prosecution such as application awaiting Board decision). Forms PTO/SB/62 and PTO/SB/63 may be used when filing a terminal disclaimer in accordance with 37 CFR 1.137(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for request for reconsideration of denial of revival (37 CFR 1.137(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reconsideration or review of a decision refusing to revive an abandoned application or lapsed patent must be filed within 2 months of the decision (or within such time set in the decision); unless indicated otherwise, this period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a renewed petition, request for reconsideration, or other petition seeking review of a prior 1.137 decision is filed outside the 1.137(e) period, the Office may require a specific showing that the entire delay was unavoidable (1.137(a)) or unintentional (1.137(b)). A deliberate decision by the applicant not to persist in seeking revival is not 'unavoidable' or 'unintentional' and remains a bar to relief; subsequent discovery of new information or changes of circumstance are immaterial to such intentional delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application revival rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.137 applies to provisional applications abandoned for failure to reply to an Office requirement, but a provisional application is regarded as abandoned 12 months after filing and is not subject to revival after that 12-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 1.137 for a provisional abandonment must be accompanied by any outstanding reply to an Office requirement because continuing-app-in-lieu-of-reply is permitted only for nonprovisional applications. A provisional may be revived pursuant to 1.137 to make it pending for at most the original 12-month period from filing; even if petition granted later, the provisional will not be pending after 12 months from its filing date. If the 12-month date falls on a weekend/holiday, pendency is extended to the next business day (35 U.S.C. 119(e)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's written statement on petition to set aside examiner's holding (37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.181, the Director may direct the examiner to furnish a written statement within a specific time setting forth reasons for his/her decision on matters averred in the petition and to supply a copy to the petitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless requested, such a statement should not be prepared. See MPEP § 1002.01 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to abandoned applications (IFW and unpublished)
rubrics_metrics.description: Access will be provided to the application file for any non-IFW abandoned published application; IFW abandoned published applications will be provided via FIU and/or Internet when IFW access is available. Access to abandoned unpublished applications may be provided if the abandoned application is identified or relied upon in a U.S. patent application publication/patent, statutory invention registration, or an international application published under PCT Article 21(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If electronic access to IFW is not available, the file-as-filed, file contents of the published application, or a specific document may be obtained by ordering a copy from the Office of Public Records upon payment of the fee in 37 CFR 1.19(b). An application is 'identified' in a patent when application number/serial number and filing date, first named inventor, title and filing date, or other application-specific information are provided in the patent text (not merely in the file contents). Form PTO/SB/68 may be used to request access under 37 CFR 1.14(a)(1)(iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pulling and forwarding abandoned application files
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandoned application files are pulled and forwarded to the Files Repository on a biweekly basis one month after the full 6-month statutory period has expired; the date of abandonment is after midnight of the date on which the shortened statutory period (including 1.136 extensions) expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should carefully scrutinize files to verify actual abandonment and check files containing Board decisions for presence of allowed claims to avoid erroneous forwarding. Although files are not pulled until the maximum permissible period (extension under 1.136(a) plus 1 month) has expired, the abandonment date is after midnight of the date the reply period actually expired (normally end of the 3-month shortened statutory period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering of patented and abandoned files (PALM/IFW procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patented and abandoned paper files are stored at the Files Repository or in off-site warehouses; Image File Wrapper (IFW) applications are stored electronically (electronic file is the official record). Files are ordered via a PALM video display transaction with status responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To order, examiner inputs PALM location code, employee number, and patent/application numbers. Response statuses: (A) accepted; (B) accepted but stored off site; (C) not accepted—file not at repository/warehouse; (D) not accepted—previous request not yet filled; (E) not accepted—invalid number. Daily PALM print transaction produces list of accepted requests; files delivered throughout day to requestors. Drawings are delivered with file to avoid separation. IFW stored electronically eliminates need for ordering/delivery process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifying applicants of abandonment and impact of not receiving notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice of Abandonment (PTOL-1432) is mailed to the correspondence address of record for applications becoming abandoned for failure to prosecute, but mere failure to receive the notice does not affect abandonment status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice procedure is intended to enable applicants to take action to reinstate inadvertently abandoned applications (often via petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137). If action is not taken promptly after receiving the notice, relief may not be granted. Failure to receive Office action or notice may indicate an address problem; applicants must promptly file a paper notifying the Office of a change of address in each application (see MPEP §§ 402 and 601.03).
